The mod-l Galois representation is a continuous homomorphism and its determinant is the cyclotomic character.

The order of vanishing of the L-series matches the rank when the rank is known independently, and the Gross-Zagier relation for a Heegner point holds numerically to the requested precision.
Sage doctests for descent and modular data.
The two-isogeny descent bound contains the actual rank, and the BSD invariants satisfy the BSD formula against independently computed L-series data.
A root of the l-th modular polynomial of E gives a curve l-isogenous to E.

The Jacobian group law satisfies the group axioms on sample divisors and the principal-divisor relation.
The Frobenius matrix characteristic polynomial matches the numerator of the zeta function obtained by direct point counting over small finite fields.
Expansion addition and multiplication agree after normalization.

Sage doctests for ciphers.
Decryption inverts encryption for every key in the key space on sample texts, and the Hill cipher's decryption matrix is the modular inverse of the key matrix.
An LFSR sequence satisfies its connection polynomial recurrence, and its linear complexity is at most the register length.
Sage doctests for block ciphers.
Decryption inverts encryption for all key sizes, and the published AES and DES test vectors are reproduced.
The polynomial system encoding a round evaluates to the same map as the procedural round on all inputs of small block size.
Sage doctests for S-boxes and Boolean functions.
The Walsh spectrum is the Fourier transform of the sign function, and the nonlinearity equals (2^n - max|Walsh|)/2.
The differential uniformity equals the maximum entry of the difference distribution table, and for AES's S-box it is 4.
Sage doctests for public-key schemes.
Decryption recovers the plaintext and every generated signature verifies against its public key.
The key exchange agrees on both sides, and an LWE sample satisfies its linear relation up to the specified error bound.
Sage doctests for polynomial system generators.
Substituting a key and plaintext into the system evaluates to the ciphertext, and the number of equations matches the block size.
Sage doctests for curve arithmetic and points.
Every returned rational point satisfies the defining equation and the count over a small finite field agrees with the Hasse-Weil bound check.
The normalization map is birational and the genus computed from the singularity data matches the function-field genus.
Sage doctests for conic solubility and parametrisation.
A returned point satisfies the conic equation, and the parametrisation map is a birational equivalence over the base field.
The Hasse principle conclusion agrees with the product of local invariants at the tested places.
Sage doctests for quartic invariants.
The invariants are unchanged by linear changes of coordinates, and each returned bitangent meets the quartic with multiplicity at least two.
Sage doctests for Jacobian construction.
The dimension of the Jacobian equals the genus of the curve, and the Jacobian of a genus-one curve is isomorphic to the curve itself.
Sage doctests for presentations of known curve complements.
The computed presentation abelianises to H_1 of the complement, and for a known curve (for example a line arrangement) it agrees with the published presentation.
Sage doctests for period matrices of known curves.
The computed period matrix is symmetric with positive-definite imaginary part, and the endomorphism ring contains the identity and is closed under composition.
Convergents satisfy the continued-fraction recurrence and the determinant identity.
Consecutive convergents bracket the represented real input with the documented error bound.
Periodic quadratic inputs reproduce their period after normalization.
Sage doctests for polyhedra.
The V- and H-representations describe the same set: every vertex satisfies every inequality and every facet contains the points it should.
The f-vector agrees with the face lattice and Euler's relation on sample polytopes; the volume agrees with the determinant formula for simplices.
Sage doctests for cones and fans.
The dual cone pairing is non-negative on generators and the double dual recovers the cone for closed cones.
The Hilbert basis generates every lattice point of the cone, and a fan morphism maps every cone into a cone of the target fan.
Sage doctests for lattice polytopes.
The normal form is invariant under unimodular transformations of the input, and the polar of a reflexive polytope is again a reflexive lattice polytope.
The Ehrhart series has palindromic numerator exactly when the polytope is reflexive.
Sage doctests for arrangements.
The characteristic polynomial evaluates to the number of regions over the reals and to the beta invariant at the appropriate values.
Deletion and restriction satisfy the deletion-restriction recurrence for the characteristic polynomial.
Sage doctests for triangulations.
The simplices of a triangulation cover the convex hull and intersect along common faces, and a regular triangulation with weights is the lower hull of the lifted configuration.
Sage doctests for Groebner fans.
The basis of a cone is a Groebner basis for the corresponding weight order, and neighbouring cones' bases are related by the Groebner walk.
Sage doctests for ribbon graphs.
Euler's relation V - E + F = 2 - 2g holds for the computed data, and the boundary components are exactly the orbits of the face permutation.
Sage doctests for Drinfeld modular forms.
Element arithmetic respects the grading, and the product of two homogeneous elements has the sum of their weights.
The constructed generators have the expected orders of vanishing at the cusp infinity.
Sage doctests for Drinfeld congruence subgroups.
The computed index agrees with N(q^deg(N) - 1) times the index of the level-one subgroup, and every returned generator reduces to a matrix congruent to the identity modulo N.
Sage doctests for dynamical systems.
Preimages of a point satisfy f(P') = P and their number equals the degree of the map, counted with multiplicity.
The canonical height is the limit of deg(f)^-n h(f^n(P)) and satisfies the functional equation h(f(P)) = deg(f) h(P) to the requested precision.
Sage doctests for sandpiles.
The stabilised configuration has each vertex below its degree and is reached by the unique legal toppling sequence, and the number of recurrent configurations equals the order of the sandpile group.
The determinant of the reduced Laplacian equals the order of the sandpile group.
Sage doctests for finite systems.
Every point is preperiodic, and the sum of cycle lengths and tree sizes equals the size of the set.
The gradient pairs with vector fields to produce the directional derivative.
The divergence of a curl vanishes in compatible coordinates.
The Euclidean Laplacian agrees with the coordinate second-derivative formula.
